abstract: We prove finite-time gradient blow-up with sharp $C^{(5-b)/(b+3)}$ H\"older regularity for a class of nonlocal transport equations extending the $b$-family, for all real $1<b<5$. This class includes the Camassa--Holm and Degasperis--Procesi equations and, after rescaling, the generalized hyperelastic-rod wave equation. In the blow-up regime, the nonlocal equations reduce at leading order to the generalized Hunter--Saxton (gHS) equation with parameter $\ell=2/(b-1)$, whose self-similar scaling and corresponding profiles depend on $\ell$. Consequently, standard approaches tailored to a fixed self-similar profile cannot be applied directly. To handle this parameter dependence, we develop a general framework for self-similar singularity formation in evolution equations whose leading-order dynamics are governed by the gHS family. The key ingredient is a family of profile inequalities established for all real $\ell>1/2$, which we combine with a generalized maximum principle to close a parameter-dependent bootstrap argument. We identify model-specific hypotheses adapted to this framework, under which this argument yields the required stability estimates. This leads to a general theorem on singularity formation, which we apply to the entire class of nonlocal equations, thereby establishing finite-time gradient blow-up and sharp H\"older regularity. The theorem can also be applied to other evolution equations once the corresponding model-specific hypotheses are verified, without repeating the profile analysis or the common stability argument.
hook: Gradient blow-up with sharp Holder regularity is proved for a whole class of nonlocal wave equations.
hook_turn: for a whole class of nonlocal wave equations.
summary: The authors prove that solutions develop infinite slopes in finite time for equations including Camassa-Holm and Degasperis-Procesi, for all b between 1 and 5. They build one framework for self-similar blow-up whose profiles depend on a parameter. The theorem needs model-specific hypotheses checked for each new equation.
title: Self-similar cusp formation in a large class of nonlocal transport equations
